original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: For two dirty rows over every finite commutative unital ring, characterize nonzero single-source-insertion feasibility by principality of the demand ideal, starting with the eight-element square-zero radical ring; prove the exact tariff for all positive stationary coefficient-independent prices.
scope_change_reason: Explicit donor assignment takes #5089 Open next question 1. This is an algebraic interface side result, not the historical helper-star H2/K implementation experiment.
bottleneck_link: Determines exactly when sharing a preserved source through reversible dirty-row mixing is feasible and its complete abstract tariff. Physical preparation/routing/precision prices, a caller and supplier admission remain missing.
stop_rule: Stop after a strict criterion and complete attaining tariff proof, or a precise counterexample; bound corroboration to nine finite rings and four full affine-state graphs, with no construction expansion.
evidence: Written arbitrary-ring-size/all-positive-price proof; exact operation-table, ideal, column-orbit, dirty-word and inverse checks; independent full-state Dijkstra comparisons with Bellman and tight-parent distance certificates. Precise finite counts are printed by verify.py; no independent human or formal-kernel acceptance claimed. Normal and optimized registered replays agree: 1761 demands, 3522 orbit comparisons, 3318 witnesses, 8601 words, 45 Dijkstra runs and 2348 optimum comparisons; 11 built-in controls and three rejected disposable semantic mutations.
author: lee-phys, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematical derivation, implementation, self-review, verification and writing. No sub-agents or independent reviewer were used.

open_questions.question: Which nonsemilocal commutative rings fail the principal-demand one-insertion criterion, or require more than four row additions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Separates principal ideal invariance from elementary-column reachability beyond stable reduction.
open_questions.first_step: Study a unimodular pair over a polynomial ring with two variables and test its elementary orbit; compare the necessary criterion with the finite-ring proof.
open_questions.blocked_by: The annihilator quotient need not have stable range one; the present finite proof supplies no orbit classification.

open_questions.question: What is the exact tariff for three dirty rows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Larger source-sharing interfaces need more than the two-row price envelope.
open_questions.first_step: Study demand (2,1,1) over Z/4 with every original dirt column retained and classify insertion supports.
open_questions.blocked_by: The two-direction return lemma does not extend unchanged when another row carries dirt.

open_questions.question: Can a concrete physical caller realize these complete abstract prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An algebraic optimum alone does not imply a supplier or exponent improvement.
open_questions.first_step: Specify and price preparation, routing, precision and restoration for one caller, then compare its completed bill.
open_questions.blocked_by: No caller or native coefficient-independent tariff matrix is supplied.
